use_cases.title: Compare publishing packages and seat availability
use_cases.description: An author compares the four paid publishing packages on `/publish` and on each package detail page to choose between package names, prices, turnaround times, feature lists, package codes, and the remaining onboarding seats in the shared monthly pool; the flow distinguishes packages that can still be chosen from ones that are fully booked, uses specific seat-availability wording including singular vs plural counts, and returns a 404 for a package that does not exist instead of failing with a generic error page.
use_cases.summary: Compare packages and current seat availability.
use_cases.value: Helps authors choose the right revenue-bearing publishing package before scarce monthly onboarding capacity is claimed.

use_cases.title: Submit a manuscript to a publishing package
use_cases.description: An author submits a manuscript into a chosen publishing package from that package's detail page by entering the book title, author name, email, genre, manuscript status, and one onboarding seat that is still available for the month; the platform must reject missing required fields, reject an unchosen manuscript-status value, reject a seat that is already taken or was never offered, suppress the form entirely when the package is fully booked, and on success create a `SUB-<n>` reference, confirm the claimed package and seat, and reduce the package's remaining monthly capacity by one.
use_cases.summary: Submit a manuscript into a package.
use_cases.value: Captures publishing demand into a paid package while enforcing limited onboarding capacity.

use_cases.title: Track and withdraw a manuscript submission
use_cases.description: An author reviews the manuscript submissions currently held for that browser session on `/my-submissions`, sees each submission's reference, book title, author, package, claimed seat, and status, and can withdraw a submission to remove it from the table, restore the package's seat to the shared monthly pool, and keep the header count synchronized with the number of submissions currently in session; this flow is session-based rather than account-based because the platform has no sign-in.
use_cases.value: Gives authors self-serve visibility into current submissions and a way to release scarce onboarding capacity.
